subject: Collaborative prompt review & ops availability for POC kickoff
messages:
From: Sam Lewis <sam.lewis@acmehealth.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC kickoff — scheduling and prompt inventory

Hi Monica —

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We're excited to move to a hands-on POC. We want to run a 3–4 hour collaborative prompt review + routing/load-testing session so our product team can validate end-to-end behavior with real prompts and expected structured outputs.

High-level asks from our side:
- Prompt inventory review (we'll share ~200 representative prompts)
- Structured output schema alignment (examples attached)
- Routing and performance expectations under 50 rps spike
- A short prep call for ops (30 min) to cover infra and guardrails

Preferred windows: Sep 7–9 (US-PDT), ideally mid-day so our EU folks can join a morning overlap if needed. Do you have a preferred slot? Also looping in procurement separately for contract timing.

Attachment: Acme-POC-requirements.pdf (stub)

Thanks,
Sam Lewis
Senior PM, Integrations — Acme Health
sam.lewis@acmehealth.com

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: Sam Lewis <sam.lewis@acmehealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — scheduling and prompt inventory

Hi Sam —

Great — we're aligned on objectives. Thanks for the clarity on scope. Proposed plan and immediate asks:

1) Workshop format (recommended):
   - 30m ops prep call (Redwood ops + Acme infra owners)
   - 3h hands-on prompt review + structured-output mapping
   - 30m wrap and next steps (rollout + load test schedule)

2) Proposed dates/times (PDT):
   - Sep 8, 10:00–14:00 (preferred)
   - Sep 9, 11:00–15:00 (backup)
   - Sep 10, 13:00–17:00 (backup 2)

3) Please share a CSV of representative prompts (prompt text, expected output, priority). I've attached our prompt-inventory-template.csv to speed this up. We also attached a short POC playbook (poc-playbook-v0.3.pdf) with runbook items and a checklist for the load window.

4) Ops note: Ben, Karthik — can you confirm GPU capacity and an available load-test window the week of Sep 7–13? We need a 2-hour controlled spike (50 rps) with KV cache warmed.

5) Procurement: Sam — if you can get procurement a target for contract signature by Sep 7 we can lock the Dedicated capacity and confirm the load-test slot.

Action items:
- Sam: drop prompt CSV + any structured-output examples by EOD Sep 3
- Ben/Karthik: confirm load-test window & capacity by EOD Sep 2
- Monica: will schedule ops prep call once Ben confirms

Attachments (stubs): prompt-inventory-template.csv, poc-playbook-v0.3.pdf

Best,
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC capacity check — Acme Health

Monica / Karthik —

Quick ops confirm: current Dedicated GPU pool has a maintenance window on Sep 8 (00:00–06:00 UTC) which should not affect the proposed daytime workshop. However, we have a heavier reserved batch job scheduled Sep 9 14:00–17:00 PDT that would reduce headroom for a 50 rps synthetic spike.

Recommended load-test slot: Sep 9 10:00–12:00 PDT or Sep 10 13:00–15:00 PDT. Sep 9 afternoon is risky unless we shift the batch job (possible but costly for the customer).

Notes for the load run:
- Warm KV cache for 30m before spike
- Use continuous batching and 4-worker shard to keep latency under 250ms p95 for typical 512-token prompts
- Quantization profile: int8 recommended for this run (we can fallback to fp16 if accuracy drops on structured outputs)

I can block the Sep 10 13:00–15:00 slot today as a safe option.

Ben
Senior Platform Ops Engineer | Redwood Inference
